headline: OpenAI Dots vs. Meta Muse AI agents compared: Big differences in price, permissions, and availability
summary: Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots offer always-on AI assistance, but their pricing tiers, data permissions, and regional availability vary significantly, with Dots starting at $100/month.
details: Both Meta Muse and OpenAI Dots are "always-on" AI agents designed to continue tasks without constant prompting. They can run cloud computers and connect to external services. Muse launched on September 8, followed by OpenAI's agents three weeks later.

Meta's Muse can handle shopping, form completion, travel plans, and email, available via its apps, web, or WhatsApp. It connects to services like email and calendar, and can organize saved social media posts into collections.

OpenAI's Dots operate within ChatGPT, powered by GPT-6 Astra, each with its own cloud computer and plugin support. They remember context and perform scheduled or recurring jobs. Users can grant Dots local computer access for files or browsing, and OpenAI plans to enable managing multiple Dots simultaneously.

A key difference is price. Muse offers a free tier with usage caps, and paid tiers at $20/month (Power) and $100/month (Maximum). OpenAI's Dots for individual users start at a much higher subscription fee, with the lowest available option being Pro 100 for $100 per month.

Both agents require supervision and permission for sensitive actions like sending emails or making purchases. Meta uses permission prompts, while OpenAI employs permissions, Custom Rules, and Auto-review, with both companies cautioning about potential mistakes. Amazon has already blocked Muse from shopping on its site.

Data usage policies also differ. Meta states Muse conversations and data within its VM are not shared with advertising systems, and users can opt out of model enhancement. OpenAI states personal-plan Dot activity may be used for model improvement depending on user settings, but Business and Enterprise data is not used for training by default.

Availability varies by region. Muse is currently available in the US and Canada. Dots are rolling out to eligible Pro users outside the European Economic Area (EEA), Switzerland, and the UK, and are available to Business Premium users across supported ChatGPT regions. Enterprise access is still in beta.

topic: android 17 data protection linked to phone price
headline_marked: [[Android 17 links data protection]] to the price of the mobile with AISeal
headline: Android 17 links data protection to the price of the mobile with AISeal
summary: Android 17's new AISeal feature processes AI tasks locally on premium phones, but budget devices must send data to Google's servers, making privacy a luxury.
details: Android 17 introduces AISeal, a hardware-isolated sandbox built on protected kernel virtual machines (pKVM). This feature is designed to execute AI tasks and keep automation data local on the device.

On expensive flagships, such as the Samsung Galaxy S26 series, AI tasks and screen analysis are performed entirely on the phone. This ensures that user data never leaves the device, enhancing privacy.

However, more affordable phones like the $499 Google Pixel 10a or Samsung Galaxy A37 lack the necessary hardware for local processing. Users of these devices must send their data and screen content to Google's remote computers to access the same automated features.
This creates a clear disparity where privacy becomes a privilege tied directly to the cost of the device. Users with cheaper phones are compelled to trust external servers with their personal data.
